newsitem.title: UK: Annual venture costs Lloyds' members dear - KPMG.
newsitem.headline: Annual venture costs Lloyds' members dear - KPMG.

text.p: The annual venture direct costs amount to more than 10 percent of the underwriting profit of insurance market Lloyd's of London and "increasingly restrict" Lloyd's competitiveness internationally, an independent report said on Friday.

The report will form part of the submission by the LCCA to the Lloyd's Syndicate Structure Working Party. The aim of this working party is to weigh the pros and cons of different capital structures for hard-hit Lloyd's Syndicates.

Chartered Accountants KPMG made the conclusions in a report submitted to the Lloyd's Corporate Capital Association (LCCA) which compared Lloyd's annual venture syndicate, which requires underwriting contracts between syndicate managers and capital providers to be reconstituted every 12 months, with limited liability companies with paid up capital.

"The direct costs associated with the management of the annual venture represent a significant proportion of a member of Lloyd's likely underwriting return, especially for traditional Names (individuals whose assets have traditionally supported the market)," the report said.

The report concluded that the maintenance of the annual venture incurs direct cost of 117 million stg in an average year, more than 10 percent of Lloyd's recently announced total underwriting profit for the 1994 year of account.

"The continuance of the annual venture is resulting in the market incurring a number of significant indirect or opportunity costs which damage the competitiveness and the efficiency of the market," the KPMG report said.
Antony Haynes, chairman of the LCCA which represents the providers of corporate capital to the Lloyd's market, said the KPMG report "speaks for itself."
"Both traditional names and corporate capital providers are seeing a substantial part of their underwriting returns being eroded by a market practice of the annual venture...," Haynes said.
